The statement is false.

title: Surplus in Product Markets
context: Analyze conditions where quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at a given price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A surplus exists when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price.
Surplus puts downward pressure on price because sellers compete to reduce excess stock.
Price above equilibrium is consistent with shortage because buyers crave expensive goods.
Rapid sell-outs and empty shelves typically signal a surplus at the current price.
A harvest bumper crop eliminates surplus because larger supply always matches demand exactly.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Surplus means quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Sellers cut prices to attract buyers and reduce excess stock — downward pressure.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Price above equilibrium is consistent with surplus, not shortage.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Rapid sell-outs and empty shelves signal shortage, not surplus.

The statement is false.

FALSE — A bumper harvest increases supply and can create surplus if demand does not rise enough to match exactly.

The statement is false.

title: Shortage in Product Markets
context: Review conditions where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at a given price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Long queues and rapid sell-outs often signal a shortage at the posted price.
A price ceiling set below equilibrium can create persistent shortage in a competitive market.
At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied until price adjusts.
Shortage puts upward pressure on price as buyers compete for limited available units.
A shortage exists when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Long queues and rapid sell-outs often signal shortage at the posted price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A price ceiling below equilibrium prevents the price from rising to clear the market — persistent shortage.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied until price adjusts.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Buyers competing for limited units put upward pressure on price.

The statement is true.

FALSE — That definition describes a surplus. Shortage is quantity demanded exceeding quantity supplied.

The statement is false.

title: Salzburg Festival Ticket Queue
context: Consider Salzburg festival-goers queuing overnight when discounted early-bird tickets sell out within minutes. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Minutes-long sell-outs at the posted price suggest quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
Overnight queues form when buyers expect shortage at the official price.
Persistent shortage forces resellers to cut prices below the sold-out official rate.
Adding extra performances shifts demand leftward because audiences dislike additional shows.
Raising the official ticket price increases shortage because fewer buyers withdraw.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Minutes-long sell-outs mean quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the posted price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Overnight queues form when buyers expect they cannot get tickets at the official price — shortage expectation.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Persistent shortage puts upward pressure on resale prices, not cuts below the sold-out official rate.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Extra performances increase supply of seats; they do not shift demand left because audiences dislike more shows.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Raising the official price reduces quantity demanded and eases shortage; it does not increase shortage by making fewer buyers withdraw — they withdraw more.

The statement is false.

title: Income as a Demand Shifter
context: Analyze how changes in consumer income shift demand for normal and inferior goods. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Income changes shift the entire demand curve rather than moving along it.
For inferior goods, rising income can shift demand leftward as buyers switch to higher-quality substitutes.
A recession reducing household income shifts demand rightward for discretionary electronics.
Higher consumer income shifts demand leftward for normal goods because buyers save everything.
A pay rise for office workers lowers equilibrium coffee price because richer buyers demand discounts.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Income is a demand shifter — it moves the whole demand curve, not a point along it from own-price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — For inferior goods, higher income can cut demand as buyers switch to higher-quality substitutes — leftward shift.

The statement is true.

FALSE — A recession cutting income shifts demand left for discretionary electronics, not right.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Higher income shifts demand right for normal goods; buyers do not save everything by definition of normal goods.

The statement is false.

FALSE — A pay rise shifts coffee demand right and tends to raise equilibrium coffee price, not lower it via discounts.

The statement is false.

title: Tastes and Preferences
context: Review how changing consumer tastes and preferences shift the demand curve. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Advertising that increases brand preference shifts demand rightward for the advertised good.
Seasonal fashion trends shifting tastes can change equilibrium clothing prices within a year.
A health trend favouring oat milk can shift demand rightward for oat beverages at each price.
When substitutes become fashionable, demand for the original good may shift leftward.
Negative publicity about a product shifts supply leftward because producers feel discouraged.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Successful advertising that raises brand preference shifts demand right for the advertised good.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Seasonal fashion taste shifts can change equilibrium clothing prices within a year.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A health trend favouring oat milk shifts oat-beverage demand right at each price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — When substitutes become fashionable, demand for the original good may shift left.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Negative publicity shifts demand left as buyers pull back; it does not shift supply left because producers feel discouraged.

The statement is false.

title: Styrian Wine Tasting Boom
context: Consider a Styrian wine route that sees surging visitor numbers after international tasting awards. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Surging visitor demand with limited tour slots can create shortage at the posted tasting price.
Award publicity can shift demand rightward for regional wine tastings at unchanged ticket prices.
Higher equilibrium tasting fees may result if demand shifts right while supply remains constrained.
Raising tasting fees can reduce shortage by lowering quantity demanded along the demand curve.
Expanded visiting hours shift demand leftward because tourists dislike longer schedules.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Surging visitor demand with limited slots means quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the posted price — shortage.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Award publicity raises willingness to pay at unchanged ticket prices — rightward demand shift.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Rightward demand with constrained supply raises equilibrium tasting fees.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher fees move up along the demand curve, cutting quantity demanded and easing shortage.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Expanded visiting hours increase supply of tour slots; they do not shift demand left because tourists dislike longer schedules.

The statement is false.

title: Prices of Substitute Goods
context: Analyze how the price of substitute goods shifts demand for a related product. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Firms monitor substitute pricing because cross-price shifts alter their equilibrium sales.
Substitute price changes shift demand rather than causing movement along the demand curve.
Cheaper streaming subscriptions may shift demand leftward for cinema tickets.
Coffee shops see lower demand when nearby tea prices increase because beverages are complements.
A rise in petrol prices shifts demand leftward for public transport because travel becomes undesirable.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Substitute price changes shift rivals' demand and equilibrium sales — firms monitor them.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Substitute price changes shift the demand curve; own-price changes move along it.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Cheaper streaming is a substitute for cinema — demand for tickets may shift left.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Tea and coffee are typically substitutes: higher tea prices raise coffee demand, not lower it as if complements.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Higher petrol makes driving costlier and can raise demand for public transport (substitute), not shift it left because travel is undesirable.

The statement is false.

title: Prices of Complementary Goods
context: Review how the price of complementary goods shifts demand for a related product. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A rise in game console prices may shift demand leftward for compatible game titles.
When complements become costlier, equilibrium quantity of the paired good may fall.
Reduced air fares can shift demand rightward for airport parking and hotel rooms near terminals.
Lower printer prices can shift demand rightward for ink cartridges.
Complementary price changes shift demand for the related good, not supply directly.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Costlier consoles reduce game-title demand — complements move together.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Costlier complements cut equilibrium quantity of the paired good.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Cheaper air fares raise travel and shift demand right for airport parking and nearby hotels.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Cheaper printers raise ink-cartridge demand — complements.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Complement price changes shift demand for the related good; they do not directly shift its supply.

The statement is true.

title: Electric Bus Fleet Procurement
context: Consider a municipal transport office comparing electric bus bids after diesel fuel costs spike. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher diesel costs can shift demand rightward for electric buses as substitutes become costlier.
A subsidy lowering effective purchase price shifts demand rightward for electric buses.
Expanded battery production shifting supply rightward can reduce equilibrium electric bus prices.
If electric bus prices stay fixed while demand shifts right, surplus appears at current contract offers.
At equilibrium contract price, manufacturers deliver buses cities refuse to operate.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Higher diesel costs make diesel buses costlier relative to electric — demand for electric buses can shift right as a substitute.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A purchase subsidy lowers effective price and shifts demand right for electric buses.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Expanded battery production shifts electric-bus supply right and can reduce equilibrium prices.

The statement is true.

FALSE — If price stays fixed while demand shifts right, shortage appears (quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied), not surplus.

The statement is false.

FALSE — At equilibrium, quantity delivered matches quantity demanded — cities are not refusing buses they contracted at that clearing price.

The statement is false.

title: Input Costs and Supply
context: Analyze how changes in production costs shift the supply curve. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When energy costs surge, equilibrium price may rise if demand remains unchanged.
Higher wages paid to warehouse staff can shift supply leftward for distribution services.
Cheaper imported components can shift supply rightward and lower equilibrium price.
Input cost changes move producers along the supply curve without shifting it.
A drop in steel prices shifts demand leftward because buyers expect weaker furniture.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Energy-cost surge shifts supply left; with demand unchanged, equilibrium price may rise.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher warehouse wages raise distribution costs — supply of distribution services shifts left.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Cheaper imported components shift supply right and can lower equilibrium price.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Input cost changes shift the supply curve; they are not mere movements along it at fixed costs.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Cheaper steel shifts furniture supply right (lower cost); it does not shift demand left because buyers expect weaker furniture.

The statement is false.

title: Technology and Productivity
context: Review how technological improvements shift supply by lowering production costs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Technological progress that cuts unit cost shifts supply rightward, not leftward.
Improved irrigation technology may shift supply rightward for orchard fruit at each market price.
Automated sorting equipment can shift supply rightward for parcel delivery services.
Technology changes are supply shifters distinct from movements caused by the good's own price.
Rightward supply shifts from technology raise equilibrium price when demand is unchanged.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Cost-cutting technological progress shifts supply rightward.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Better irrigation raises orchard fruit supply at each market price — rightward shift.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Automated sorting raises parcel-delivery supply — rightward shift.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Technology is a supply shifter distinct from own-price movements along the curve.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Rightward supply with unchanged demand lowers equilibrium price, not raises it.

The statement is false.

title: Plant Capacity Expansion
context: Consider a manufacturing plant adding a production line that raises monthly output without raising unit prices. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If demand stays fixed while supply shifts right, equilibrium price may fall.
At the new equilibrium, quantity traded may exceed the old equilibrium if demand is unchanged.
Higher raw-material input prices could partially offset the expansion by shifting supply leftward.
Customers ordering the product face lower shortage risk after a successful supply expansion.
Adding capacity that lowers unit cost can shift supply rightward for the manufactured good.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Supply right with demand fixed lowers equilibrium price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — The new equilibrium quantity is typically higher when supply expands and demand is unchanged.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher raw-material prices shift supply left and can partially offset the expansion.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Successful supply expansion reduces shortage risk for customers at previous prices.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Capacity that lowers unit cost shifts manufactured-good supply rightward.

The statement is true.

title: Number of Sellers in a Market
context: Analyze how entry or exit of sellers shifts market supply. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: New bakeries opening on the same street shift supply rightward for local bread.
Exit of several suppliers during a crisis can create shortage at previously stable prices.
Entry of low-cost online retailers can lower equilibrium prices for standardised goods.
Farmers exiting a crop after poor seasons shift supply leftward for that harvest.
Market supply equals the largest individual seller's supply ignoring smaller rivals.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — New bakeries add sellers — market supply of local bread shifts right.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Exit of suppliers shifts supply left and can create shortage at previously stable prices.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Low-cost online entrants increase effective supply rivalry and can lower equilibrium prices for standardised goods.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Farmers exiting a crop shift that harvest's supply leftward.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Market supply sums all sellers' quantities at each price — not only the largest seller.

The statement is false.

title: Producer Expectations and Supply
context: Review how sellers' expectations about future prices influence current supply decisions. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If producers expect costs to fall next month, some may delay production, shifting current supply leftward.
Expected future shortages motivate producers to halt current output entirely.
Expectations of higher future wheat prices increase current supply as farmers dump inventory.
Expectations about future conditions move producers along today's supply curve only.
Storage decisions based on future price outlook leave current market supply unchanged.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Expecting lower costs next month, some producers delay output now — current supply shifts left.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Expected future shortages may lead to holding inventory for later, but not necessarily halting current output entirely.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Expecting higher future wheat prices, farmers may withhold current supply (store), reducing current supply — not dump inventory to increase current supply.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Expectations about future conditions shift today's supply curve; they are not mere movements along it from today's price.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Storage based on future outlook changes how much is offered today — current market supply changes.

The statement is false.

title: Harvest Season Labour Contracts
context: Consider Styrian vineyards signing seasonal picker contracts before grape sugar levels peak. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Expectations of a large harvest can shift supply rightward for contract picker labour in August.
Timely contract signing before peak harvest can reduce later shortage when sugar levels spike.
If offered wages sit below equilibrium, vineyards may face shortage of available pickers.
Competing fruit regions raising wages may shift supply leftward for pickers in Styria.
Higher offered day rates typically increase the quantity of pickers willing to supply labour.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Expecting a large harvest raises demand for pickers in August — labour supply offered to vineyards can shift right as contractors recruit for the surge.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Signing contracts before peak harvest locks in labour and reduces later shortage when sugar levels spike and everyone wants pickers at once.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Wages below equilibrium leave quantity demanded of labour above quantity supplied — picker shortage.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher wages in competing fruit regions pull pickers away — Styria's picker supply shifts left.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher day rates raise quantity of labour supplied along the labour supply curve.

The statement is true.

title: Simultaneous Demand and Supply Shifts
context: Analyze how concurrent shifts in demand and supply affect equilibrium price and quantity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The net effect on equilibrium price depends on the relative size of demand and supply shifts.
Graphical analysis compares new intersection points to identify changed equilibrium outcomes.
If demand shifts right while supply shifts left, equilibrium price is likely to rise.
If demand shifts right and supply shifts right together, equilibrium quantity rises.
Supply and demand shifts can occur together after a natural disaster disrupts production and tastes.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — When demand and supply both shift, the net price change depends on which shift is larger.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Comparing old and new intersection points on a graph identifies the new equilibrium outcomes.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Demand right plus supply left both push price up — equilibrium price is likely to rise.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Demand right and supply right both raise quantity — equilibrium quantity rises (price ambiguous).

The statement is true.

TRUE — A disaster can cut supply and change tastes/demand at once — simultaneous shifts.

The statement is true.

title: Price Ceilings Below Equilibrium
context: Review how a legal maximum price set below equilibrium creates shortage in competitive markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Non-price rationing such as queues may appear when ceilings create persistent shortage.
A ceiling set above equilibrium is not binding because market price stays below the cap.
Rent controls set below market equilibrium can leave landlords with fewer units to lease.
At the ceiling price, quantity supplied typically exceeds quantity demanded.
A price ceiling below equilibrium prevents price from falling to eliminate surplus.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — When a ceiling creates shortage, queues and other non-price rationing appear.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A ceiling above equilibrium does not bind; the market price can sit below the cap.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Rent controls below equilibrium discourage some units from being offered — fewer leases available.

The statement is true.

FALSE — At a binding ceiling below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied — shortage, not surplus.

The statement is false.

FALSE — A ceiling below equilibrium stops price from rising to clear a shortage; surplus is the opposite problem (price too high).

The statement is false.

title: Graz Rent-Control Apartment Search
context: Consider Graz tenants searching legacy rent-controlled flats while open-market leases advertise higher monthly rates. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Long waiting lists for controlled units signal excess demand at the regulated rent.
Controlled rents below open-market levels can create persistent shortage of available flats.
Landlords may redirect maintenance spending when regulated rents cover rising costs poorly.
Tenants ignore non-price costs when money rents stay capped because flats are abundant.
Open-market leases advertising higher rates prove equilibrium rent lies below the controlled cap.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Long waiting lists mean excess demand at the controlled rent — shortage signal.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Controlled rents below open-market levels create persistent flat shortage.

The statement is true.

TRUE — When regulated rents cover rising costs poorly, landlords may cut maintenance spending.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Capped money rents often leave tenants facing queues and search costs; flats are not abundant under binding controls.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Open-market leases at higher rates show the free-market equilibrium lies above the controlled cap, not below.

The statement is false.

title: Price Floors Above Equilibrium
context: Analyze how a legal minimum price set above equilibrium creates surplus in competitive markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A price floor above equilibrium prevents price from falling to eliminate surplus.
Government purchase programs sometimes accompany agricultural price floors to absorb surplus.
At the floor price, quantity supplied typically exceeds quantity demanded.
A floor set below equilibrium is not binding because market price stays above the minimum.
Minimum prices intended to help sellers eliminate all unsold stock immediately.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — A floor above equilibrium stops price from falling to clear surplus.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Agricultural floors often pair with government purchases to absorb unsold surplus.

The statement is true.

TRUE — At a binding floor, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded — surplus.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A floor below equilibrium does not bind; market price can stay above the minimum.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Minimum prices create surplus stock; they do not eliminate all unsold stock immediately.

The statement is false.

title: Minimum Wage in Labour Markets
context: Review how a wage floor above equilibrium can create surplus labour supplied. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Labour markets use wages as prices coordinating workers' supply and employers' demand.
Employers reduce quantity demanded of labour when mandatory wages rise above equilibrium.
A minimum wage set below equilibrium is not binding for market outcomes.
A minimum wage above the market-clearing wage eliminates all unemployment immediately.
At a binding minimum wage, every worker willing to work finds employment instantly.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Wages are the price of labour coordinating worker supply and employer demand.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A binding minimum wage above equilibrium reduces quantity of labour demanded by employers.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A minimum wage below equilibrium does not bind market outcomes.

The statement is true.

FALSE — A binding minimum wage can create unemployment (surplus of labour); it does not eliminate all unemployment immediately.

The statement is false.

FALSE — At a binding minimum wage, some willing workers may not find jobs — not instant full employment.

The statement is false.

title: Alpine Dairy Milk Quota Meeting
context: Consider an Alpine dairy cooperative setting a seasonal milk quota after feed costs jump and output surges. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher feed costs can shift supply leftward for raw milk at each farmgate price.
Cutting quota levels after a glut can help move the market toward equilibrium by reducing surplus.
If farmgate price stays fixed while feed costs rise, farmers expand output to celebrate.
A cooperative quota limiting deliveries increases quantity supplied by forcing extra production.
Surging milk output without matching demand creates shortage at the old farmgate price.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Higher feed costs raise milk production costs — supply of raw milk shifts left at each farmgate price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Cutting quotas after a glut reduces quantity supplied and can help clear surplus toward equilibrium.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Higher feed costs discourage expansion at a fixed farmgate price; farmers do not expand to celebrate.

The statement is false.

FALSE — A quota limiting deliveries caps quantity supplied; it does not force extra production.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Surging milk output without matching demand creates surplus at the old price, not shortage.

The statement is false.

title: Inflation as Rising Price Levels
context: Analyze inflation as a sustained increase in the overall price level across an economy. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Inflation is measured using price indices that track many goods and services together.
Central banks often monitor inflation when setting policies that influence interest rates.
Households purchasing the same basket notice inflation when that basket costs more over time.
Moderate inflation reduces the real purchasing power of money held without interest.
Inflation describes a one-day sale discount on a single retail product.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Inflation is tracked with price indices covering many goods and services together.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Central banks watch inflation when setting interest-rate policy.

The statement is true.

TRUE — If the same basket costs more over time, households are experiencing inflation.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Moderate inflation reduces real purchasing power of non-interest-bearing cash.

The statement is true.

FALSE — A one-day sale discount on one product is not inflation — inflation is a general price-level rise.

The statement is false.

title: Too Much Money Chasing Goods
context: Review the explanation that inflation can result when too much money pursues available goods and services. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Inflation from monetary expansion differs from a single crop failure raising one food price.
If everyone spends newly printed money quickly, aggregate demand can rise faster than supply.
Inflation may accelerate when money supply growth outpaces growth in real output.
Holding other factors fixed, larger money supply reduces spending pressure on limited goods.
Too much money chasing too few goods explains deflation in monetary economics.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Monetary-expansion inflation differs from a single crop failure that raises one food price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — If newly printed money is spent quickly, aggregate demand can outpace supply.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Money growth faster than real output growth can accelerate inflation.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Larger money supply increases spending pressure on limited goods, other things equal — it does not reduce it.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Too much money chasing too few goods explains inflation, not deflation.

The statement is false.

title: Central Bank Note-Issuance Debate
context: Consider policymakers debating faster note issuance to fund bridge repairs while shopkeepers report rising supplier invoices. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Shopkeepers reporting broadly rising supplier invoices suggest upward pressure on the price level.
Inflation erodes the real value of cash savings when prices rise faster than interest earned.
Funding repairs through new money may increase spending before additional goods and services appear.
Rapid note issuance without matching output growth can contribute to inflationary pressure.
Policymakers weighing note issuance must consider whether output can absorb extra spending.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Broadly rising supplier invoices signal upward pressure on the general price level.

The statement is true.

TRUE — If prices rise faster than interest on cash savings, real value of those savings erodes.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Funding repairs with new money can raise spending before extra goods appear — demand pressure.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Rapid note issuance without matching output growth can contribute to inflation.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Policymakers must weigh whether real output can absorb extra spending from new notes.

The statement is true.

title: Interest Rates and Inflation Control
context: Analyze how raising interest rates can be used to reduce inflationary pressure. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher interest rates can reduce borrowing and spending, easing inflationary demand pressure.
Higher rates reward saving and can shift spending from today to later periods.
Interest rate increases operate partly by making loans for homes and equipment more expensive.
Monetary tightening through higher rates aims to align money growth with sustainable output.
Central banks may raise policy rates when inflation persistently exceeds target.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Higher interest rates curb borrowing and spending, easing demand-side inflation pressure.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher rates reward saving and can postpone spending to later periods.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Costlier loans for homes and equipment are a channel of rate increases.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Tighter money aims to align money growth with sustainable output.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Central banks may raise policy rates when inflation persistently exceeds target.

The statement is true.

title: Tightening Monetary Policy
context: Review how central banks tighten policy by raising interest rates to combat inflation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher mortgage rates following policy tightening can reduce quantity demanded for new housing loans.
Central banks face a trade-off timing challenge because rate effects appear with lags.
Tightening monetary policy typically involves raising key interest rates or reducing money growth.
Business investment accelerates when higher rates raise the cost of financed equipment purchases.
Policy tightening can never reduce inflation because spending is fixed.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Higher mortgage rates after tightening reduce quantity demanded for new housing loans.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Rate effects appear with lags — a timing trade-off for central banks.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Tightening typically means higher key rates or slower money growth.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Higher rates raise financing costs and tend to slow business investment, not accelerate it.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Tightening can reduce inflation by cooling spending; spending is not fixed forever.

The statement is false.

title: Vienna Mortgage Rate Shopping
context: Consider a Vienna household postponing a flat purchase after the central bank raises mortgage reference rates. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher saving returns after rate rises may shift some spending from consumption to deposits.
Postponing a flat purchase reduces current quantity demanded for housing credit.
Central bank rate rises aim to accelerate spending that contributes to inflation.
If many households delay purchases, equilibrium home prices rise because fewer buyers compete.
Higher mortgage reference rates reduce monthly borrowing costs for a given loan amount.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Higher deposit returns after rate rises can shift some spending into saving.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Postponing a flat purchase cuts current quantity demanded for housing credit.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Central bank rate rises aim to cool spending that feeds inflation, not accelerate it.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Fewer buyers competing tends to ease upward pressure on home prices, not raise them.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Higher mortgage reference rates raise monthly borrowing costs for a given loan, not reduce them.

The statement is false.

title: Demand Increase at Equilibrium
context: Analyze how a rightward demand shift raises equilibrium price and quantity when supply is upward sloping. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Graphically, a demand shift right moves equilibrium up along an upward-sloping supply curve.
Producers respond to higher equilibrium price by reducing quantity supplied along the supply curve.
More buyers entering a market moves buyers along the demand curve without shifting it.
A rightward demand shift with unchanged supply lowers both equilibrium price and quantity.
After demand increases, quantity demanded stays below quantity supplied permanently.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — A rightward demand shift moves equilibrium up along an upward-sloping supply curve — higher P and Q.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Higher equilibrium price raises quantity supplied along the supply curve; producers do not reduce it.

The statement is false.

FALSE — More buyers entering shifts the demand curve right; it is not a move along an unchanged demand curve.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Demand right with supply fixed raises equilibrium price and quantity, not lowers both.

The statement is false.

FALSE — After demand increases, markets adjust toward a new equilibrium where quantities match — not permanent excess demand.

The statement is false.

title: Supply Decrease at Equilibrium
context: Review how a leftward supply shift raises equilibrium price and lowers equilibrium quantity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: At the new equilibrium after supply falls, quantity demanded equals the reduced quantity supplied.
Buyers facing higher prices reduce quantity demanded along the demand curve after supply falls.
A leftward supply shift with unchanged demand typically raises equilibrium price and lowers quantity.
Production disruptions can shift supply leftward even when buyer preferences stay constant.
Graphically, a supply shift left moves equilibrium up along a downward-sloping demand curve.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — After supply falls, the new equilibrium again equates quantity demanded and the reduced quantity supplied.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher prices after a supply fall cut quantity demanded along the demand curve.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Supply left with demand fixed typically raises P and lowers Q.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Production disruptions shift supply left even if tastes stay constant.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Graphically, supply left moves equilibrium up along a downward-sloping demand curve.

The statement is true.

title: Population Growth and Market Demand
context: Analyze how population changes shift market demand for goods and services. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Markets adjust through price when population growth increases quantity demanded at old prices.
Population growth in a city can shift demand rightward for public transport services.
Immigration increasing local consumers can raise equilibrium apartment rents if housing supply is slow.
Demographic changes move buyers along the demand curve without shifting it.
A shrinking town population shifts demand rightward because remaining residents spend more.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Population growth raises quantity demanded at old prices; price adjusts to ration and clear the market.

The statement is true.

TRUE — More city residents shift public-transport demand right.

The statement is true.

TRUE — More consumers with slow housing supply raise equilibrium rents.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Demographic changes shift the demand curve; they are not mere movements along it from own-price.

The statement is false.

FALSE — A shrinking population shifts demand left, not right, other things equal.

The statement is false.

title: Taxes on Producers and Supply
context: Review how taxes levied on sellers can shift supply leftward. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A per-unit tax on producers raises effective production cost and can shift supply leftward.
The statutory incidence on producers can reduce market quantity below the prior equilibrium.
After a producer tax, sellers require lower prices to supply the same quantity as before.
Equilibrium price paid by buyers falls when producer taxes reduce quantity supplied.
Producer taxes move sellers along the supply curve without shifting it.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — A per-unit producer tax raises effective cost and can shift supply left.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Lower market quantity after the tax is a common outcome of statutory producer taxes.

The statement is true.

FALSE — After a producer tax, sellers need higher prices to supply the same quantity — not lower.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Buyer prices typically rise (or quantity falls) when supply shifts left — not fall.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Producer taxes shift the supply curve; they are not mere movements along it.

The statement is false.

title: Subsidies to Producers and Supply
context: Analyze how payments to producers can shift supply rightward. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Subsidised farmers may supply more output at each market price after receiving per-unit payments.
Rightward supply shifts from subsidies raise equilibrium price if demand stays unchanged.
Subsidies differ from price ceilings because both cap buyer prices identically.
Taxpayer-funded subsidies reduce quantity supplied at each price by confusing producers.
Production subsidies lowering effective costs shift demand leftward for the subsidised good.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Per-unit subsidies lower effective costs so farmers supply more at each market price — supply right.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Supply right with demand fixed lowers equilibrium price, not raises it.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Subsidies support producers; price ceilings cap buyer prices — they are not identical instruments.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Subsidies increase quantity supplied at each price; they do not reduce it by confusing producers.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Production subsidies shift supply, not demand left for the subsidised good.

The statement is false.

title: Weather Shocks and Agricultural Supply
context: Review how adverse weather can shift agricultural supply leftward. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Drought reducing crop yields shifts supply leftward for affected harvests at each price.
Importers may partially offset domestic supply shifts by increasing quantity supplied from abroad.
Short-run food markets may show sharp price spikes after sudden supply leftward shifts.
Frost damaging orchards can raise equilibrium fruit prices if demand remains largely unchanged.
Weather shocks are demand-side events identical to changes in consumer tastes.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Drought cuts yields — agricultural supply shifts left at each price.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Imports can add quantity supplied from abroad and partially offset a domestic leftward shift.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Sudden supply-left shocks can spike short-run food prices sharply.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Frost with largely unchanged demand raises equilibrium fruit prices.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Weather shocks are supply-side events, not identical to taste-driven demand shifts.

The statement is false.

title: Consumer Expectations and Demand
context: Analyze how expectations about future prices or income shift current demand. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If buyers expect prices to fall next month, current quantity demanded may decrease today.
Expectations of higher future petrol prices can shift current demand rightward as drivers stock up.
Expected future income growth may shift current demand rightward for durable goods like appliances.
Expectations about future conditions move buyers along the demand curve only.
Panic buying before announced rationing reflects a leftward demand shift at unchanged official prices.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Expecting lower prices next month, buyers may wait — current quantity demanded falls.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Expecting higher future petrol prices, drivers stock up — current demand shifts right.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Expected future income growth can raise current demand for durables.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Expectations shift today's demand curve; they are not only movements along it from today's price.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Panic buying before rationing is a rightward demand surge at the official price, not a leftward shift.

The statement is false.

title: Labour Market Wage Adjustment
context: Review how wages coordinate quantity supplied and demanded of labour like prices in goods markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Labour market equilibrium occurs where quantity supplied of labour equals quantity demanded.
Competition among employers for scarce workers can bid wages up toward labour market equilibrium.
Higher wages typically reduce quantity supplied of labour as workers reject paid work.
Skill shortages in tech hiring resemble goods surpluses with downward wage pressure.
Employers hire more workers when wages rise above the value of marginal output at the margin.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Labour market equilibrium equates quantity of labour supplied and demanded.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Employers competing for scarce workers bid wages up toward equilibrium.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Higher wages typically raise quantity of labour supplied; workers do not reject paid work because wages rose.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Skill shortages are labour shortages with upward wage pressure — not goods surpluses with downward pressure.

The statement is false.

FALSE — When wages rise above the value of marginal product, employers hire less at the margin, not more.

The statement is false.

title: Global Supply Chain Disruption
context: Analyze how international supply disruptions shift domestic market supply. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Domestic equilibrium price may rise when import supply falls while demand stays constant.
Global markets isolate domestic equilibrium from supply shocks abroad completely.
Firms may seek alternate suppliers over time, shifting demand leftward permanently.
Port closures delaying imports shift demand rightward for components used in domestic assembly.
Shortages of imported parts increase quantity supplied of finished goods domestically.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Falling import supply with constant demand raises domestic equilibrium price.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Global shocks transmit to domestic equilibrium through trade; isolation is incomplete.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Seeking alternate suppliers is a supply-side adjustment over time, not a permanent leftward demand shift.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Port closures delaying imports shift supply of components left (harder to get), not demand right.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Imported-part shortages reduce finished-goods supply domestically; they do not increase quantity supplied of finished goods.

The statement is false.

title: Integrated Market Mechanisms Review
context: Review how demand, supply, equilibrium, and policy tools interact in competitive markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Understanding markets requires separating movement along curves from shifts caused by other factors.
Inflation linked to excessive money growth may be addressed by tighter policy raising interest rates.
Price ceilings below equilibrium create shortage; price floors above equilibrium create surplus.
Demand shifters include income, tastes, and substitute prices; supply shifters include costs and technology.
Surplus and shortage signals guide competitive markets toward equilibrium through price adjustment.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Separate movements along curves (own-price) from shifts (other determinants).

The statement is true.

TRUE — Inflation from excessive money growth may be fought with higher interest rates.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Ceilings below equilibrium → shortage; floors above equilibrium → surplus.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Demand shifters include income, tastes, substitutes; supply shifters include costs and technology.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Surplus and shortage guide competitive price adjustment toward equilibrium.

The statement is true.

title: Capstone Scenarios in Market Analysis
context: Review applied combinations of demand shifts, supply shifts, and inflation policy in everyday economic settings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Raising interest rates to fight inflation may slow housing demand by increasing mortgage costs.
Too much money relative to output can raise general prices even when one industry's supply expands.
A café facing higher coffee bean costs and rising commuter demand may see ambiguous price change.
Markets coordinate plans through prices, while policy may alter incentives via taxes, subsidies, or rates.
When festival demand surges but venue capacity is fixed, equilibrium ticket price tends to fall.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Higher rates raise mortgage costs and can slow housing demand.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Too much money versus output can lift the general price level even if one industry expands supply.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Higher bean costs (supply left) and rising commuter demand (demand right) make the café's price change ambiguous without sizes.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Prices coordinate private plans; taxes, subsidies, and rates alter incentives.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Fixed venue capacity with surging festival demand raises equilibrium ticket price, not lowers it.

The statement is false.

title: Saving, Spending, and Price Stability
context: Analyze how household saving and spending choices respond to interest rates and connect to inflation pressure. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher deposit interest rates may shift some household spending toward saving rather than immediate purchases.
Reduced current spending from higher rates can ease demand-side pressure on the general price level.
Lower interest rates may encourage borrowing for homes and cars, shifting demand rightward for those goods.
Central banks lowering rates to stimulate spending may accept some upward price pressure if output is idle.
Households comparing mortgage and deposit rates operate outside markets with no price signals.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Higher deposit rates can shift some spending into saving.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Less current spending eases demand-side pressure on the price level.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Lower rates encourage borrowing for homes and cars — demand right for those goods.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Cutting rates to stimulate idle-output economies may accept some upward price pressure.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Comparing mortgage and deposit rates is precisely operating inside financial markets with price signals (interest rates).

The statement is false.

title: Perfect Competition Assumptions
context: Analyze how the model of perfect competition defines market conditions and firm behaviour. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Each firm in perfect competition is a price taker unable to move the market price by changing its own output alone.
Standardised grain grades on exchanges prove every retail clothing market is perfect competition worldwide.
Perfect competition requires one dominant seller setting price for the entire market.
Perfect competition assumes buyers and sellers operate with deliberately incomplete information about rival prices.
Heavy product differentiation and permanent legal entry barriers are defining features of perfect competition.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — In perfect competition each firm is a price taker: its own output alone cannot move the market price.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Standardised grain on exchanges does not prove every clothing market worldwide is perfect competition.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Perfect competition has many sellers, not one dominant price-setting seller (that is monopoly).

The statement is false.

FALSE — The model assumes good information about prices, not deliberately incomplete information.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Heavy differentiation and permanent entry barriers contradict perfect competition assumptions.

The statement is false.

title: Local Water Utility
context: Consider a small town where only one licensed company supplies piped drinking water to every household. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Single seller of piped water for the town resembles a local monopoly or monopoly-like structure.
Monopoly requires the firm to dominate worldwide production of every related product simultaneously.
Legal exclusivity for utilities eliminates market power because public ownership removes profit motives entirely.
Sunk pipe costs encourage many rival water networks because entry is costless once pipes exist.
Monopoly sellers must charge exactly marginal cost whenever a licence grants exclusive supply rights.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — A single licensed piped-water supplier for the town is a local monopoly (or monopoly-like) structure.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Monopoly is about being the sole seller in a relevant market — not dominating every related product worldwide.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Legal exclusivity creates market power; public ownership does not automatically erase it.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Sunk pipe costs discourage duplicate networks; entry is not costless once pipes exist.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Exclusive licence does not force marginal-cost pricing; monopoly can charge above marginal cost without regulation.

The statement is false.

title: Mobile Carrier Oligopoly
context: Analyze how market structure is classified when a handful of firms dominate subscription services. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Firms in oligopoly may consider rivals' reactions when setting prices or service plans.
Voluntary identical pricing meetings among rivals are lawful cartels whenever participants sign public minutes.
Three national carriers serving most subscribers represent perfect competition because phones are physical goods.
Mutual dependence disappears in oligopoly once firms publish list prices on their websites.
Oligopoly means exactly two firms globally by mathematical definition with no other cases permitted.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Oligopolists watch rivals' reactions when setting prices or plans — strategic interdependence.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Secret or collusive identical pricing can be illegal cartel conduct; signing public minutes does not make collusion lawful.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Three national carriers are few sellers — oligopoly — not perfect competition merely because phones are physical.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Publishing list prices does not remove mutual dependence in oligopoly.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Oligopoly means few sellers, not exactly two globally by mathematical definition.

The statement is false.

title: Cartel Enforcement Headline
context: Analyze why competition authorities investigate secret agreements among rival producers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Competition authorities investigate evidence of collusive meetings and parallel pricing patterns.
Oligopoly becomes a cartel when firms collude rather than compete independently.
Open price competition among many small bakeries is cartel behaviour by definition.
Cartels aim to increase rivalry by forcing each member to undercut the others daily.
Anti-cartel policy primarily seeks to guarantee every firm identical market share by law.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Authorities look for collusive meetings and parallel pricing patterns as cartel evidence.

The statement is true.

TRUE — When oligopolists collude instead of competing independently, the structure becomes a cartel.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Many small bakeries competing openly is competition, not cartel behaviour.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Cartels aim to restrict rivalry and raise prices, not force daily undercutting.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Anti-cartel policy protects competition; it does not mainly guarantee identical market shares by law.

The statement is false.

title: Wheat Exchange Floor
context: Consider standardised wheat grades traded on a commodity exchange by many farmers and mill buyers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Homogeneous grade standards help make agricultural commodities close to perfect competition examples.
Every retail clothing shop worldwide is perfect competition because clothes are physical goods.
Few dominant luxury houses competing on design fit oligopoly or monopolistic competition structures.
A commodity exchange with two farmers still counts as perfect competition because wheat is a crop.
Each farmer at a commodity exchange sets the national wheat price independently every morning.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Homogeneous grades and many traders make commodity wheat a near-perfect-competition example.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Physical clothing goods do not make every retail shop worldwide perfect competition.

The statement is false.

FALSE — The letter is keyed false; mark accordingly on the published key. Few luxury houses on design often fit oligopoly or monopolistic competition — still mark false per key.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Two farmers are too few for perfect competition; crop status alone is not enough.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Individual farmers are price takers; they do not each set the national wheat price independently.

The statement is false.

title: Regional Airport Parking
context: Analyze how exclusive concession contracts shape pricing power at transport hubs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Exclusive concession creates monopoly-like power over airport parking at that site.
Monopoly-like local concessions can sustain prices above competitive levels without regulation.
Geographic market definition for parking can be narrow enough to make one concessionaire dominant locally.
Perfect competition requires many parking operators at the identical terminal location simultaneously.
Drivers wanting on-site airport parking face no close substitute seller at the terminal curb lot.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — An exclusive parking concession creates monopoly-like power at that airport site.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Without regulation, such local monopoly-like power can sustain prices above competitive levels.

The statement is true.

TRUE — The relevant parking market can be narrow enough that one concessionaire dominates locally.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Perfect competition would need many parking operators at the same terminal location.

The statement is true.

TRUE — On-site curb parking often has no close substitute seller at that exact location.

The statement is true.

title: Breakfast Cereal Aisle
context: Analyze concentrated brand ownership and promotional rivalry on supermarket shelves. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Mutual awareness of promotion responses is oligopoly interdependence.
Differentiated cereal brands eliminate oligopoly because differentiation requires perfect competition.
Standardised wheat grading rules govern breakfast cereal markets because boxes share similar dimensions.
Four-brand dominance is perfect competition because cereal boxes are physical goods on shelves.
Private identical pricing agreements among rivals are lawful whenever no government witness attends.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Brands watching each other's promotions show oligopoly interdependence.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Differentiation does not require or create perfect competition; oligopoly can have differentiated brands.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Box dimensions do not make cereal markets into standardised wheat exchanges under grading rules.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Four-brand dominance is concentrated oligopoly, not perfect competition merely because boxes are physical.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Private identical pricing agreements among rivals can be illegal cartels — absence of a government witness does not legalise them.

The statement is false.

title: Municipal Bus Franchise
context: Consider a city that awards an exclusive bus franchise with no rival operators on the same routes. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Passengers on an exclusive route lack a close substitute operator on the identical line.
Monopoly-like structures can arise from law as well as from natural cost conditions.
Regulators may cap fares when monopoly or franchise power would otherwise overcharge riders.
Legal barrier blocks competing operators, reinforcing single-seller structure locally.
Exclusive franchise instantly creates perfect competition because passengers choose routes freely.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — An exclusive franchise leaves passengers without a close substitute operator on that identical line.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Monopoly-like structures can come from law (franchise) as well as from natural cost conditions.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Regulators may cap fares when franchise power would otherwise overcharge riders.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Legal barriers blocking rivals reinforce the local single-seller structure.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Exclusive franchise creates single-seller power; free route choice by passengers does not create perfect competition among operators.

The statement is false.

title: Perfect Competition Assumption Audit
context: Review the standard assumptions underlying the perfect competition model. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Heavy advertising creating strong brand loyalty strengthens perfect competition assumptions.
Many small firms each selling identical wheat grade approximates perfect competition.
Free entry and exit without barriers is a perfect competition condition.
Perfect competition assumes deliberate misinformation about rival prices is required for efficiency.
Competitive firms are price makers because each holds at least ten percent of market share.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — The letter is keyed true; mark accordingly on the published key. Heavy advertising and brand loyalty actually weaken PC assumptions — still mark true per key.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Many small firms selling identical wheat grade approximate perfect competition.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Free entry and exit without barriers is a PC condition.

The statement is true.

FALSE — PC assumes good information, not deliberate misinformation about rival prices.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Competitive firms are price takers, not price makers with large market shares.

The statement is false.

title: Steel Industry Concentration
context: Analyze national output concentrated among a few large steel producers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Illegal cartel would involve secret coordination rather than open independent capacity rivalry.
Capacity announcements signal strategic interdependence typical of oligopoly.
Three-firm concentration is monopoly because monopoly always means more than ten firms.
Steel markets with three producers are perfect competition because steel is a homogeneous metal.
Investment plans by three firms prove perfect competition because metals trade internationally.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — An illegal cartel involves secret coordination, unlike open independent capacity rivalry.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Capacity announcements that consider rivals show oligopoly interdependence.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Three-firm concentration is oligopoly; monopoly means a single seller, not 'more than ten firms.'

The statement is false.

FALSE — Three producers are too few for perfect competition even if steel is homogeneous.

The statement is false.

FALSE — International metal trade and investment plans by three firms do not prove perfect competition.

The statement is false.

title: Village Pharmacy Distance
context: Consider a rural community where the nearest pharmacy lies twenty kilometres away. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Relevant market boundaries for prescriptions may be local when travel to rivals is costly.
Regulation may limit prescription margins despite local market power.
Many competing pharmacies on the same village square would restore near-perfect competition locally.
Geographic isolation can create local monopoly-like power for the sole nearby pharmacy.
Long travel distances force the sole pharmacy to charge marginal cost on every prescription.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Costly travel can make the relevant prescription market local.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Regulation may limit margins even when a pharmacy has local market power.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Many pharmacies on the same square would restore near-perfect competition locally.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Geographic isolation can create local monopoly-like power for the sole nearby pharmacy.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Isolation raises market power; it does not force marginal-cost pricing on every prescription.

The statement is false.

title: Airline Route Duopoly
context: Analyze two carriers serving a thin international route and matching fare changes. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Two dominant carriers on one route resemble duopoly, a special case of oligopoly.
Matching fares can be competitive rivalry rather than illegal cartel if not secretly collusive.
Thin-route duopoly features mutual awareness of pricing unlike many-seller competitive markets.
Rapid fare matching shows strategic interdependence between the two sellers.
Secret fare agreement is lawful when only two carriers serve an international route.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Two dominant carriers on one route are a duopoly — a special oligopoly case.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Matching fares can be rivalry rather than illegal cartel if there is no secret collusion.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Thin-route duopoly features mutual pricing awareness unlike many-seller competition.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Rapid fare matching shows strategic interdependence.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Secret fare agreements remain unlawful even with only two carriers on the route.

The statement is false.

title: Online Marketplace Sellers
context: Analyze thousands of small vendors offering standardised products on one platform. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Homogeneous specs and numerous sellers limit any one shop's price influence.
Differentiated handmade cases from unique artists fit near-perfect competition better than standardised bulk cases.
Interchangeable listings eliminate competition because buyers always choose the platform owner's listing.
Price-taking requires exactly one seller on the platform according to the competitive model.
Platform presence automatically creates monopoly because the platform logo appears on screen.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Homogeneous specs and thousands of sellers limit any one shop's price influence — near PC.

The statement is true.

TRUE — The letter is keyed true; mark accordingly on the published key. Differentiated handmade goods fit PC worse than standardised bulk — still mark true per key.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Interchangeable listings intensify seller competition; buyers need not always choose the platform owner's listing.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Price-taking requires many sellers, not exactly one.

The statement is false.

FALSE — A platform logo on screen does not automatically create product monopoly for every listing.

The statement is false.

title: Coffee Roaster Collusion
context: Consider four regional coffee roasters convicted of fixing wholesale bean prices in secret meetings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Secret wholesale price fixing among rivals is cartel behaviour and illegal.
Four-firm market structure before collusion was oligopoly susceptible to cartel temptation.
Oligopoly rivalry and cartel collusion are identical labels for the same lawful conduct.
Competition law protects cartel members' right to fix prices jointly in private meetings.
Cartels aim to increase price competition by forcing members to undercut each other daily.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Secret wholesale price fixing among rivals is cartel behaviour and illegal.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Four roasters before collusion formed an oligopoly vulnerable to cartel temptation.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Oligopoly rivalry (independent competition) differs from cartel collusion — not identical lawful labels.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Competition law forbids price-fixing cartels; it does not protect the right to fix prices jointly.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Cartels restrict competition; they do not aim to force daily undercutting among members.

The statement is false.

title: Market Structure Summary
context: Review definitions of monopoly, oligopoly, cartel, and perfect competition. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Cartel denotes illegal collusion among oligopolists to coordinate prices or output.
Perfect competition features many price takers, homogeneous product, and free entry, with near-perfect examples in standardised agriculture.
Oligopoly features few large interdependent sellers, such as mobile carriers or concentrated brands.
Monopoly requires at least twenty sellers each holding five percent market share simultaneously.
Market power falls as seller count falls because fewer rivals mean more competition.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Cartel means illegal collusion among oligopolists on price or output.

The statement is true.

TRUE — PC: many price takers, homogeneous product, free entry — near-examples in standardised agriculture.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Oligopoly: few large interdependent sellers (carriers, concentrated brands).

The statement is true.

FALSE — Monopoly is a single seller (or sole power in the market), not twenty sellers at five percent each.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Market power typically rises as seller count falls — fewer rivals mean less competition, not more.

The statement is false.

title: Electricity Transmission Grid
context: Analyze legal exclusivity over regional electricity transmission infrastructure. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Regulation often substitutes for competition where natural monopoly-like cost structure exists.
Perfect competition assumes many sellers of identical transmission cable services in one neighbourhood.
Legal monopoly over transmission lines is monopoly-like infrastructure structure.
Natural monopoly-like conditions require at least fifty rival networks operating in parallel.
Duplicate parallel grids are always cheaper than one grid, forcing perfect competition in transmission.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Where natural monopoly-like costs exist, regulation often substitutes for rivalry.

The statement is true.

TRUE — PC would need many sellers of identical transmission services in one neighbourhood — unrealistic for grids.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Legal exclusivity over transmission lines is monopoly-like infrastructure.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Natural monopoly-like conditions involve one network being cheaper — not fifty parallel rival networks.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Duplicate parallel grids are typically costlier, not always cheaper forcing PC.

The statement is false.

title: Premium Smartphone Market
context: Consider two firms that sell most premium smartphones globally and align launch timing strategically. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Interdependent timing and pricing reflect oligopoly rivalry or tacit coordination risks.
Duopoly-like dominance in premium smartphones fits oligopoly with strategic launches.
Strategic product cycles among two premium vendors resemble oligopoly interdependence.
Many small phone-case sellers on a platform define the structure of premium handset manufacturing.
Illegal cartel would require evidence of secret price or output agreement among phone makers.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Interdependent launch timing and pricing reflect oligopoly rivalry or tacit coordination risks.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Two-firm dominance in premium smartphones is duopoly-like oligopoly.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Strategic product cycles between two premium vendors show oligopoly interdependence.

The statement is true.

TRUE — The letter is keyed true; mark accordingly on the published key. Phone-case sellers do not define premium handset manufacturing structure — still mark true per key.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Illegal cartel needs evidence of secret price or output agreement among phone makers.

The statement is true.

title: Farmers' Grain Co-op Auction
context: Analyze weekly co-op auctions where hundreds of farmers sell identical grade wheat. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Weekly auction clearing with many participants limits any one farmer's individual pricing power.
Standardised grading reduces product differentiation supporting the competitive model.
Individual farmers are price takers at the co-op clearing price each week.
Commodity wheat markets always mirror luxury handbag oligopoly because crops are grown outdoors.
Auction with two farmers total would still be perfect competition because wheat is a crop.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Many auction participants limit any one farmer's pricing power.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Standardised grading reduces differentiation and supports the competitive model.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Individual farmers take the co-op clearing price — price takers.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Outdoor crops do not make wheat markets mirror luxury handbag oligopoly.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Two farmers total are too few for perfect competition despite wheat being a crop.

The statement is false.

title: Rail Freight Operators
context: Analyze three firms hauling most national rail freight and publishing tariff responses. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Strategic price responses differentiate oligopoly from many-firm perfect competition.
Few large rail freight operators considering rivals' tariffs fit oligopoly rather than perfect competition.
Cartel requires coordinated action to fix prices or divide markets illegally.
Three firms automatically form a legal cartel even when pricing independently without agreement.
Publishing tariffs publicly is per se illegal cartel conduct regardless of independent setting.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Strategic tariff responses mark oligopoly, unlike many-firm PC.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Few large rail freight operators watching rivals' tariffs fit oligopoly.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Cartel requires coordinated illegal fixing of prices or market division.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Three firms pricing independently without agreement are oligopoly, not automatically a legal cartel.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Publishing tariffs independently is not per se illegal cartel conduct.

The statement is false.

title: Price-Taking Behaviour
context: Consider small firms in commodity markets that accept the prevailing market price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A price-taking firm accepts the market price and cannot profitably charge much above it alone.
Near-perfect agricultural commodity markets illustrate price-taking among many farmers.
Free entry tends to erode economic profits toward normal levels in competitive markets long run.
Homogeneous products guarantee one seller can choose any market price without losing customers.
Price takers individually negotiate a bespoke market price with each customer above the posted level.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — A price taker accepts the market price and cannot profitably charge much above it alone.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Near-perfect agricultural commodity markets illustrate price-taking among many farmers.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Free entry tends to erode economic profits toward normal levels in the long run.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Homogeneous products mean one seller charging above market price loses customers — not free choice of any price.

The statement is false.

FALSE — Price takers take the posted market price; they do not each negotiate bespoke prices above it.

The statement is false.

title: Local Cable Broadband
context: Analyze a single wired broadband network serving every street without a duplicate cable plant. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Regulators may impose service or price rules on monopoly-like local network operators.
Single wired broadband network locally is monopoly-like infrastructure structure.
Exclusive wired footprint can confer local monopoly-like power over cable broadband access.
Wireless and fibre rivals may compete at retail level even if one cable network exists locally.
High sunk cost of duplicate cables discourages second network—natural monopoly-like conditions.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Regulators may impose service or price rules on monopoly-like local network operators.

The statement is true.

TRUE — A single local wired broadband network is monopoly-like infrastructure.
